prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: Real-time translation of worship exists, but no translator preserves theological nuance between faith vocabularies, so the Main KPI of 2,000,000,000 believers with access is unmet. The Vatican began AI live translation of Mass into 60 languages with Translated's Lara in 2026 (https://translated.com/holy-mass-translated-with-ai), and spf.io serves congregations with custom terminology (https://repo.uum.edu.my/id/eprint/32587/). Faith-aware terminology exists only within single traditions, e.g. Vurbo.ai with a 10,000-term Buddhist lexicon (https://journalofcyberpolicy.com/?p=311773). Studies of LLM translation of hadith, Quran and Islamic texts find recurring failures on theological terms and cultural context and call for expert review (https://opde.journals.ekb.eg/article_384369.html, https://asjp.cerist.dz/en/article/284900). Terminology-constrained MT assumes one-to-one term mappings, which concepts such as grace, dharma or tawhid lack (https://api.emergentmind.com/topics/terminology-constrained-machine-translation). Honest limit: within-tradition liturgy translation is a known answer; cross-faith nuance preservation is open, but there is no agreed metric for it, so tasks need expert-attested evaluation sets first.
